# leptos_aria

> Headless accessible components for Leptos, ported from React Aria with the Radix/shadcn primitive surface completed. No styles ship; state is exposed as `data-*` attributes for Tailwind v4. A shadcn-style CLI copies styled wrapper components into your project.

Install the library, install the CLI, add components:

```
cargo add leptos_aria
cargo install leptos_aria_cli --path crates/leptos_aria_cli
leptos-aria add button
```

## Docs

- [Tailwind v4 guide](docs/tailwind.md): styling states with `data-[state=open]` variants and `@custom-variant` blocks, plus the full data-attribute contract
- [Registry](registry/registry.json): the shadcn-schema component manifest the CLI reads
- [Porting roadmap](PORTING.md): every upstream hook, utility, and component with its crate
- [API docs](https://docs.rs/leptos_aria): the facade crate on docs.rs

## The data-attribute contract

Every interactive component exposes its state so styling stays external:

- `data-state`: `open`/`closed` (Modal, Popover, Tooltip, AlertDialog, HoverCard, ContextMenu, Accordion), `checked`/`unchecked` (Switch), `on`/`off` (ToggleGroup), `selected` (Calendar, Tabs, ListBox), `loaded`/`fallback` (Avatar)
- `data-disabled`, `data-dragging`, `data-is-dragging`, `data-current`, `data-orientation`, `data-action`, `data-focused`, `data-expanded`

Tailwind v4's built-in `data-[...]` and `aria-*` variants target these directly with no plugin.

## Component surface

Interactions: usePress, useFocus, useFocusWithin, useHover, useFocusable, useFocusRing, useKeyboard, useLongPress, useMove, useDrag/useDrop, useScroll, useDismiss, useModal, FocusManager, useAutofocus.

Components: Button, AnchorButton, CustomButton, ToggleButton, ToggleGroup, Switch, Form, TextField, TextArea, SearchField, NumberField, OneTimePasswordField, Checkbox, CheckboxGroup, RadioGroup, Slider, ComboBox, SelectBox, ListBox, Menu, MenuTrigger, ContextMenu, Menubar, Tabs, TagGroup, Toolbar, Tooltip, Popover, Modal, AlertDialog, Dialog, HoverCard, Calendar, DatePicker, DateField, DateRangePicker, TimeField, FileTrigger, Grid, Table, Tree, Meter, ProgressBar, Toast, DropZone, DraggableItem, Link, Breadcrumb, Heading, Text, VisuallyHidden, Disclosure, Accordion, Pagination, ScrollArea, Separator, AspectRatio, Avatar, ColorField, ColorArea, ColorSlider, ColorWheel, ColorSwatch.

## Registry CLI

`leptos-aria init` writes the config; `leptos-aria add <name>` copies styled wrappers (your files, Tailwind classes) that depend on the headless crates; `leptos-aria list` names the registry.

# Full documentation

## readme

# leptos_aria

> A port of the `react-aria` ecosystem for the leptos framework.

## Motivation

[`leptos`](https://github.com/leptos-rs/leptos) is an amazing rust web framework. It is still in its infancy and needs to better accessibility support.

This is an attempt to provide a port of the `react-aria` ecosystem to `leptos`.

## Contributing

[`devenv`](https://devenv.sh/) is used to provide a reproducible development environment for this project. Follow the [getting started instructions](https://devenv.sh/getting-started/).

To automatically load the environment you should [install direnv](https://devenv.sh/automatic-shell-activation/) and then load the `direnv`.

```bash
# The security mechanism didn't allow to load the `.envrc`.
# Since we trust it, let's allow it execution.
direnv allow .
```

At this point you should see the `nix` commands available in your terminal.

To setup recommended configuration for your favourite editor run the following commands.

```bash
setup:vscode # Setup vscode
setup:helix  # Setup helix configuration
```

## Development

The following scripts are available inside the devenv shell.

```bash
build:all   # build every crate for the wasm32 target
fix:all     # run dprint fmt and cargo clippy --fix
lint:all    # run dprint check and cargo clippy
test:all    # run the native and wasm32 browser test suites
test:wasm   # run the browser test suite only
```

The browser tests run through `wasm-bindgen-test-runner` with a local Chrome driven by `chromedriver`; both come from the devenv shell. The `wasm-bindgen` dependency is pinned to the `wasm-bindgen-cli` version in the devenv lock so the runner and the crate always match.


## Tailwind v4 guide

# Tailwind CSS v4

Every component is headless: no styles ship, and state is exposed as `data-*` attributes so Tailwind's arbitrary variants style it directly. No plugin, no configuration, no dependency — add the crate, style with the classes you already write.

## Style with arbitrary variants

Tailwind v4 supports `data-[...]` variants out of the box:

```rust
use leptos_aria::Accordion;

view! {
	<Accordion>
		<AccordionItem key="one".to_string()>
			<AccordionTrigger class="data-[state=open]:bg-slate-100 font-medium">
				"Section"
			</AccordionTrigger>
			<AccordionPanel class="data-[state=open]:animate-in">
				"Content"
			</AccordionPanel>
		</AccordionItem>
	</Accordion>
}
```

## Or name the variants once

A short `@custom-variant` block in your CSS turns every state into a one-word variant:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@custom-variant open (&:where([data-state="open"], [data-state="checked"], [data-state="on"]));
@custom-variant closed (&:where([data-state="closed"], [data-state="unchecked"], [data-state="off"]));
@custom-variant disabled- (*:disabled, &:where([data-disabled="true"]));
```

```html
<button class="open:bg-slate-100 closed:bg-white disabled-:opacity-50" />
```

## The attribute contract

| Attribute          | Values                    | Where                                                                                      |
| ------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `data-state`       | `open` / `closed`         | Modal, Popover, Tooltip, AlertDialog, HoverCard, ContextMenu, Accordion item/trigger/panel |
| `data-state`       | `checked` / `unchecked`   | Switch                                                                                     |
| `data-state`       | `on` / `off`              | ToggleGroupItem                                                                            |
| `data-state`       | `selected`                | Calendar cells, Tabs, ListBox options                                                      |
| `data-state`       | `loaded` / `fallback`     | Avatar                                                                                     |
| `data-disabled`    | `true` / `false`          | Accordion item, overlay triggers                                                           |
| `data-dragging`    | `true` / `false`          | DropZone                                                                                   |
| `data-is-dragging` | `true` / `false`          | DraggableItem                                                                              |
| `data-current`     | `true`                    | Pagination page buttons                                                                    |
| `data-orientation` | `horizontal` / `vertical` | Separator, Toolbar                                                                         |
| `data-action`      | `cancel` / `confirm`      | AlertDialog buttons                                                                        |
| `data-focused`     | `true` / `false`          | ListBox options, Tabs                                                                      |
| `data-expanded`    | `true` / `false`          | ComboBox                                                                                   |

Alongside the ARIA attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-selected`, ...), Tailwind v4's built-in `aria-*` variants cover the rest: `aria-pressed:bg-blue-500` needs no extra code.


## Porting roadmap

# Porting roadmap

A direct port of the [`react-aria`](https://react-spectrum.adobe.com/react-aria/) ecosystem to [`leptos`](https://leptos.dev), one interaction and one component at a time. Each entry links to the upstream source it mirrors; the crate column names where the port lives.

Status legend: **done** (ported and tested), **planned** (not started).

## Interactions

| Hook                  | Status | Crate                                        |
| --------------------- | ------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| `usePress`            | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_press`        |
| `useFocus`            | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_focus`        |
| `useFocusWithin`      | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_focus_within` |
| `useHover`            | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_hover`        |
| `useFocusable`        | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_focusable`    |
| `useFocusRing`        | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_focus_ring`   |
| `useKeyboard`         | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_keyboard`     |
| `useLongPress`        | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_long_press`   |
| `useScroll`           | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_scroll`       |
| `useDrag` / `useDrop` | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions`                   |
| `useMove`             | done   | `leptos_aria_interactions::use_move`         |
| `useDismiss`          | done   | `leptos_aria_overlay::use_overlay_dismiss`   |
| `useModal`            | done   | `leptos_aria_overlay::use_modal`             |

## Porting conventions

- One crate per component family, matching the workspace layout, with a single `leptos_aria` facade crate re-exporting everything; crate names use underscores (`leptos_aria_name`).
- Hooks take a `...Props` builder struct and return a `...Result` carrying the props to spread onto the target element, mirroring the upstream `useX(props) -> {xProps}` shape.
- Upstream refs become `Rc`/`Arc`-shared state structs whose handler methods are wrapped as cloneable callbacks.
- Upstream module-level singletons (`textSelection`, transition tracking, interaction modality) become thread-local state.
- Callbacks are boxed `dyn Fn` in props and `Rc`/`Arc`-wrapped internally; event payloads that upstream wraps (press, hover, focus) become small owned structs carrying the resolved target.
- React-specific polyfills (synthetic blur via `MutationObserver`, the React 16 `PointerEvent` fallbacks) are adapted or noted in code comments where the platform no longer needs them.
